messages:
sophie: observed a weird billing spike on a customer flow — streaming request got routed -> model-v1 then retried to model-v2 and the toolcall payload looks like it was truncated then retried, customer saw double token charge.

tony: ugh. so the router changed mid-stream? any router logs?

sophie: looks like it. router did an opaque reroute on capacity pressure. logs show stream-start routed to eu-west, then a reconnect routed to eu-north. kv cache miss + new model variant caused truncation of streaming toolcall. snippet: 
```
[2024-06-12T15:02:11Z] stream.start id=abc123 route=eu-west model=rw-13b-v1
[2024-06-12T15:02:13Z] connection.reset id=abc123 reason=evicted
[2024-06-12T15:02:13Z] stream.resume id=abc123 route=eu-north model=rw-13b-v2 truncated=true
```

maya: hmm truncated=true is the kicker. we bill on tokens produced; if the resumed stream produced additional tokens and the toolcall also replayed, that can double-count.

elaine: do we currently associate charges to a route session id or to the public request id only?

sam: charges are per-request id, but streaming segments are charged per-session + per-emitted-token. router reassignment creates a new session id which our billing side considers a new emission unless dedupe metadata is present.

tony: so bug is router creating a new session without preserving enough dedupe/continuation metadata for billing?

sophie: yeah. quick repro: start a streaming toolcall that emits a toolcall event mid-stream, trigger a router failover, force resumed model variant. Billing ledger shows both the partial toolcall from v1 and final toolcall from v2 as charged. customer sees 2x for the same logical toolcall.

maya: short-term mitigation: have the router attach original_request_id and original_charge_id to resumed sessions so billing can dedupe within a small window. long-term: prefer sticky routing for in-flight streams to avoid mid-stream variant changes.

elaine: console UX question: should we show provisional credits for resumptions? Ops asked if we can surface provisional "reconciled" charges so support can explain to customers.

sam: billing-bot can emit provisional entries but reconciliation will be async. risk: support noise and confusing invoices. alternative: reconcile automatically and only surface final charges in the console, but show reconciliation timeline + reason in the trace.

tony: implementation plan suggestion: 1) router to propagate original_request_id + continuity_flag; 2) billing to dedupe by original_request_id for streaming toolcalls for N=30s; 3) console: show "reconciled" badge on any charge adjusted within 24h.

maya: performance/complexity notes: adding dedupe lookups on hot path increases latency. maybe implement a cheap in-memory cache in billing-proxy keyed by original_request_id to map to charge_id, then fall back to async reconcilers.

sophie: also need to handle model-variant differences: if resumed stream produced fewer tokens because v2 truncates differently, reconciliation must subtract the earlier provisional charge. there are edge cases where content differs and we shouldn't dedupe blindly.

elaine: +1 to a small window and manual audit flags. we'll draft a support playbook: how to explain reconciled adjustments and where to look in logs.

sam: i'll wedge a quick prototype for billing-proxy dedupe this sprint. assigned: sam. router change tracked in PR #480.

billing-bot: NOTE: created billing-issue BI-1724 for investigation and customer outreach template. :eyes:

sophie: thanks. will add a short repro script and sample trace to BI-1724.

tony: sounds good. follow-ups: can we add a smoke test that forcibly reroutes in-flight streams and asserts single logical charge? low-friction test would catch regressions.

maya: agreed, I'll add test to the routing-integration suite.

sophie: ok closing loop here for now. if anyone hits more repros drop them in BI-1724 or ping me directly. :slightly_smiling_face:
